items.title: Russia fires Oreshnik missile in massive assault on Kyiv

featured_image.name: Russia launched Oreshnik missile at Kyiv Oblast in overnight attack ...

items.description:
Russia unleashed one of its most devastating aerial assaults on Kyiv since the full-scale invasion began, firing 90 missiles and 600 drones at the Ukrainian capital and surrounding areas overnight Sunday, killing at least four people and wounding more than 80, according to Ukrainian officials.[1][2]

Multiple rounds of explosions were heard across the city throughout the early morning hours in a bombardment that lasted more than five hours, damaging residential buildings, schools, markets, and a trade center across the capital.[3][4]

items.title: Zelensky calls Germany's associate EU membership plan 'unfair'

featured_image.name: Exclusive-Ukraine's Zelenskiy says proposal of associate EU ...

items.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky told EU leaders in a letter sent late on Friday that a German proposal to grant Ukraine "associate" membership of the European Union was "unfair" because it would leave Kyiv without a voice inside the bloc, according to Reuters, which reviewed the message.[1][2]

"It would be unfair for Ukraine to be present in the European Union, but remain voiceless," Zelensky wrote. "The time is right to move forward with Ukraine's membership in a full and meaningful way."[2][1]

items.title: US naval blockade of Iran hits 100 redirected ships

featured_image.name: CENTCOM boasts month-long Iran naval blockade, redirecting 67 commercial  ships

items.description:
U.S. Central Command announced on Friday that American forces have redirected more than 100 commercial vessels since the naval blockade of Iranian ports began on April 13, marking a milestone in the six-week-old maritime operation designed to choke off Tehran's oil exports.[1][2]

The achievement comes as CENTCOM steadily escalated its enforcement figures — from 37 ships redirected by April 25, to 58 by May 8, 67 by May 12, 85 by May 18, and 94 as of May 21 — underscoring the pace of commercial traffic still attempting to reach Iranian waters despite the blockade.[3][4][5][6][7]

items.title: Rubio invites Modi to White House amid trade impasse

featured_image.name: Marco Rubio holds talks with PM Modi during Delhi…

items.description:
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi in New Delhi on Saturday, extending a White House invitation on behalf of President Donald Trump as Washington seeks to stabilize a relationship frayed by trade disputes and competing geopolitical pressures.[1][2]

Rubio's four-day visit — his first official trip to India — comes as the two countries navigate a complicated trade landscape shaped by court rulings that dismantled much of Trump's tariff architecture and new investigations that could reimpose duties on Indian goods.
